title: civica household writing guide
status: authored guide; source scope and implementation boundaries apply

normative_levels.MUST: Required civica content contract within its stated scope. Not a claim of law or universal native HA conformance.
normative_levels.SHOULD: Default; exceptions need a recorded reason and verification.
normative_levels.MAY: Permitted contextual choice; mandatory contracts still apply.

pages.title: Writing for a connected home
pages.description: A practical writing standard for civica household controls, states, help and documentation.

pages.title: Voice and language
pages.description: Use calm, precise household language that stays truthful under stress and uncertainty.

pages.title: Words and style
pages.description: Choose consistent household terms while preserving native labels, user names and exact identifiers.

pages.title: Interface copy and truthful states
pages.description: Write controls, confirmations and missing states that match what Home Assistant actually supports and knows.

pages.title: Errors, warnings and notifications
pages.description: Explain recovery and urgency without inventing causes, capabilities or safety assurances.

pages.title: Instructions, questions and learning
pages.description: Write useful task steps and forms with clear prerequisites, honest examples and relevant help.

pages.title: Inclusive household content
pages.description: Respect different households, languages and abilities while protecting presence and personal information.

pages.title: Numbers, dates and household data
pages.description: Preserve units, precision, missing readings and time context in values, charts and comparisons.

pages.title: Accessible content
pages.description: Use structure, meaningful alternatives and clear interaction text, informed by SCULPT.

pages.title: Review and maintain content
pages.description: Record evidence, exceptions and meaningful changes without overstating what was checked.

rules.title: Start with a real household need
rules.requirement: State who needs the content, what they need to do or understand, and the context in which they will use it.
rules.check: A short user need identifies the task and audience; content that does not help that need is removed.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Apply the guide to content we own
rules.requirement: Change civica-authored labels and explanatory content without silently rewriting native Home Assistant translations, user names or integration values.
rules.check: The change identifies owned strings; native labels, user text and literal values remain intact.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Use requirement levels deliberately
rules.requirement: Interpret MUST as a required civica content contract, SHOULD as a tested default with a documented reason for an exception, and MAY as an allowed contextual choice.
rules.check: Each exception names its rule, reason, scope and verification; normative terms are not mistaken for legal obligations.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Keep source-system claims in their proper scope
rules.requirement: Adapt transferable writing principles without importing clinical assurance, government identity, legal rules or unsupported services.
rules.check: No content claims endorsement, clinical review, emergency monitoring, translation provision or a household capability without evidence.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Use familiar, concrete language
rules.requirement: Prefer the shortest familiar wording that preserves the technical meaning and necessary conditions.
rules.check: A reader can identify the device, state or action without translating unnecessary jargon.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Match certainty to the evidence
rules.requirement: Qualify estimates, last reported states and unconfirmed outcomes; do not turn them into facts by simplifying the wording.
rules.check: Every assertion of completion, cause, presence or safety has a defined source and confirmation condition.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Be calm without false reassurance
rules.requirement: Use neutral, respectful language and give useful context instead of humour, blame, panic or unsupported reassurance.
rules.check: Failure and high-consequence messages remain factual and identify an appropriate next step.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Make sentences easy to follow
rules.requirement: Prefer one main idea per sentence, an explicit actor when useful, and short paragraphs with meaningful headings.
rules.check: A read-aloud review finds clear actors, actions and conditions; sentences are shortened without losing qualifiers.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Expand contractions where clarity matters
rules.requirement: Use cannot, do not and other expanded forms in critical conditions, warnings and short task instructions; use positive contractions only when they remain clear for the audience.
rules.check: Important negative conditions are easy to distinguish, translate and read aloud.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Treat readability scores as diagnostic tools
rules.requirement: Do not present a reading-age score, sentence count or automated language check as proof that people understand the content.
rules.check: Review includes task comprehension and relevant user feedback, with automated measures described as limited checks.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Use a small, deliberate household vocabulary
rules.requirement: Choose consistent authored terms for the same operation and different terms for different operations.
rules.check: A terminology review maps each verb to an actual operation and finds no contradictory synonyms.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Preserve native labels and translations
rules.requirement: Use the actual Home Assistant label for a feature, setting or control when referring people to it, in the language of that interface.
rules.check: Instructions and authored help match the supported interface version and locale; native strings are not rewritten by styling.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Respect names supplied by people
rules.requirement: Display names as supplied, including meaningful spelling, case, punctuation and language; distinguish a display-name edit from an identifier change.
rules.check: Names remain unchanged across cards, dialogs, confirmations and accessible names.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Use sentence case and restrained punctuation
rules.requirement: Use sentence case for authored English headings and labels, conventional UK English spelling, and punctuation that helps meaning.
rules.check: Headings and controls avoid block capitals and unnecessary punctuation while proper names remain intact.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Explain necessary abbreviations at the point of need
rules.requirement: Expand unfamiliar abbreviations when first needed and provide a short practical explanation of a technical term.
rules.check: A new reader can understand the term without leaving the task; repeated expansions do not overwhelm compact controls.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Keep literal values literal
rules.requirement: Preserve the exact syntax, case and meaningful punctuation of entity IDs, codes, paths, version strings and values someone needs to copy.
rules.check: Displayed and copied literal values match the supplied source; prose punctuation is outside the value.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Name the action and its object
rules.requirement: Use a concrete verb and enough context to identify the effect of a control.
rules.check: The label remains understandable in its visible context and accessible name.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Separate state from action
rules.requirement: Label a current or last reported state separately from the operation a button requests.
rules.check: An On or Off state cannot be mistaken for the action taken by activating the control.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Distinguish a request from a confirmed result
rules.requirement: Only claim completion when the integration’s documented confirmation condition is met; distinguish sending, acceptance, reported state and lack of confirmation.
rules.check: Tests cover accepted requests without a state change, reported success, rejection and timeout.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Keep unavailable, unknown, stale and offline distinct
rules.requirement: Describe missing information using the actual source state and timestamp; claim offline only when connection evidence supports it.
rules.check: Unknown and unavailable values are not rendered as zero, off, safe or definitely disconnected; retained readings are labelled with their time.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Explain actual capability and permission limits
rules.requirement: Offer only supported actions and explain a relevant restriction without claiming that the interface can grant device or account permissions.
rules.check: Unsupported actions are absent; disabled supported actions have an accurate reason and a verified next step where one exists.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Distinguish saved, enabled and running
rules.requirement: Describe configuration persistence, future automatic starts and current execution as separate states.
rules.check: Copy for automations, schedules and scenes does not imply that saving, enabling or selecting one has the same effect.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Describe cancellation and destructive effects precisely
rules.requirement: State what Cancel, Stop, Remove and Delete affect, including any operation that may continue or cannot be undone.
rules.check: Confirmation text names the target and consequence; cancellation outcomes match what the implementation actually cancels.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Set a truthful destination expectation
rules.requirement: Identify external services, downloads and changes of context when they affect a person’s choice; do not disguise device actions as navigation.
rules.check: Links lead to the stated destination; downloads have accurate type and available size; new-window behaviour is disclosed when necessary.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Make questions and empty states unambiguous
rules.requirement: Give each input a visible label, explain necessary formats and conditions, and distinguish no results from missing data or access restrictions.
rules.check: Labels, hints and validation are associated with their controls; each empty state gives the right reason and supported next step.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Give a recovery supported by the known cause
rules.requirement: Name the affected task and explain an available next step without inventing a diagnosis, retained work or a successful retry.
rules.check: Every recovery action has an implementation or verified destination; promises about saved input and recovery are tested.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Distinguish validation from service failure
rules.requirement: Use a field error for a correctable answer, a task-level message for a failed request, and status copy for unavailable information.
rules.check: A person is not asked to correct a valid answer because the network, integration or permission check failed.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Choose urgency from evidence
rules.requirement: Use severity words and presentation only for a defined condition, keeping informational records, required actions and immediate hazard signals distinct.
rules.check: The content names its source condition and does not classify ordinary maintenance data as a live emergency.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Respect the boundary of household safety information
rules.requirement: Do not claim that Home Assistant replaces a physical safety check, certified alarm, qualified advice or an authoritative emergency procedure.
rules.check: Safety-related wording has a named evidence source and appropriate review; no unverified procedure or medical claim is added.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Explain pending and uncertain outcomes
rules.requirement: Keep a pending message distinct from failure and success, and explain when an operation may still complete after the interface stops waiting.
rules.check: Slow, interrupted, partial and timed-out operations have accurate copy and do not encourage unsafe duplicate requests.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Keep notifications truthful and private
rules.requirement: Adapt message detail to the supported delivery channel, intended recipient and shared-screen context without changing the underlying meaning.
rules.check: Notifications avoid unnecessary location, identity and sensitive household detail; channels and recipients exist and are authorised by the implementation.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Avoid blame and alarm fatigue
rules.requirement: Keep errors factual, avoid repeated announcements of unchanged problems, and reserve assertive interruptions for genuinely urgent information.
rules.check: Messages remain understandable without blame, exaggerated punctuation or repeated identical alerts.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Order instructions around the task
rules.requirement: Put necessary preparation first, use numbered steps for a sequence, and keep each step centred on one action or decision.
rules.check: A person can follow the steps in order without searching backwards for a prerequisite.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: State real prerequisites and consequences
rules.requirement: Explain required permissions, supported capabilities and significant effects before the person commits to the task.
rules.check: Preparation and consequence text matches the actual implementation, including remote-control requirements and destructive effects.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Refer to the actual interface
rules.requirement: Use verified control names and supported navigation for the stated version, and identify when an illustration is a simplified example.
rules.check: Steps are checked against the target interface or explicitly marked reference-only; screenshots do not invent controls.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Give useful help near the decision
rules.requirement: Place essential conditions and short format hints next to the relevant question; put optional explanation in a clearly named details section.
rules.check: A person can answer safely without opening a tooltip or following a generic help link.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Ask only necessary questions
rules.requirement: Use a question protocol that records purpose, who must answer, validation, optionality and what happens when an answer is missing.
rules.check: Each question is justified and tested; unnecessary personal information and repeated questions are removed.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Support learning without overloading the task
rules.requirement: Introduce concepts in the order people need them and use worked examples that connect a control to its effect.
rules.check: Help explains unfamiliar concepts without requiring memorised identifiers, long uninterrupted instructions or irrelevant technical background.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Keep examples and alternative formats honest
rules.requirement: Label synthetic data, illustrative controls and unavailable formats; do not imply that a prototype performs a live action or supplies a translation that does not exist.
rules.check: Examples state their scope, local actions remain local, and every advertised download, video or alternative format is available and reviewed.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Avoid unnecessary assumptions about people
rules.requirement: Do not infer relationships, ownership, gender, age, technical ability or physical access when the task does not establish them.
rules.check: Copy works for different household arrangements and does not assign a task by stereotype.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Ask for personal information only when needed
rules.requirement: Collect and display only the identity or household detail required for the stated task, and explain a sensitive question’s purpose.
rules.check: Forms and messages justify sensitive fields and offer a meaningful alternative where the service supports one.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Use respectful, specific language
rules.requirement: Use the person’s stated name and relevant self-description; avoid labels, euphemisms and stereotypes that define someone by an assumed condition.
rules.check: Content is checked with the intended audience and respects self-description without collecting unnecessary identity data.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Avoid assuming one way to perceive or act
rules.requirement: Write directions that work without relying on colour, vision, hearing, a pointer or a particular physical ability.
rules.check: Instructions identify controls by name and purpose and include verified alternatives when the task needs them.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Describe BSL and other formats accurately
rules.requirement: Only advertise a signed or translated version when that version exists, matches the content and has the appropriate quality review.
rules.check: Format links resolve to actual content with a known version and review; captions, transcripts and BSL are not presented as interchangeable.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Preserve language and translation integrity
rules.requirement: Preserve native locale behaviour and supplied names, identify authored translations honestly, and do not treat machine translation as validated content.
rules.check: Critical translations receive appropriate human review; language metadata is correct and sensitive text is not sent to unapproved external tools.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Treat presence as sensitive and uncertain
rules.requirement: Describe tracker-derived presence as a reported or inferred state, and limit personal detail on shared displays and notifications.
rules.check: Presence wording names the evidence and time where relevant; privacy claims match what the display actually hides.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Name the measured quantity
rules.requirement: Identify the quantity and distinguish rates, totals, settings, estimates and reported measurements.
rules.check: Labels match the source metadata and do not interchange power, energy, temperature, target temperature or cost.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Preserve meaningful precision
rules.requirement: Do not round, convert or calculate a displayed value in a way that changes its meaning or implies greater accuracy than the source supports.
rules.check: Display precision, conversions and derived values are documented and do not alter the underlying data.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Respect number and date preferences
rules.requirement: Use Home Assistant’s configured locale, number format, clock and time-zone preferences for dynamic values.
rules.check: Tests include a language/number-format mismatch, 12- and 24-hour preferences and the supported time-zone choices.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Keep units attached to their values
rules.requirement: Show the correct unit or a clearly associated column or axis unit, and preserve the distinction between similarly named units.
rules.check: Values remain interpretable when read aloud, in a table or outside the surrounding chart.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Identify the time represented by data
rules.requirement: Label an observation time, interval start, interval end or selected period according to the actual data model.
rules.check: A chart/table timestamp is not described as period start when it represents a sample or midpoint.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Make ambiguous times and schedules explicit
rules.requirement: Explain the relevant time zone and boundaries when a schedule, comparison or repeated clock time could be misunderstood.
rules.check: Tests cover a zone difference and daylight-saving changes where the feature supports affected dates.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Preserve missing readings and real zeros
rules.requirement: Show a missing, unknown or unavailable value as missing; preserve a genuine zero and identify incomplete totals.
rules.check: Tables, charts and summaries distinguish null, zero, gaps and incomplete coverage.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Give charts equivalent context and readable data
rules.requirement: Provide a meaningful title, quantity, period and accessible data alternative that describes the same values and uncertainty as the chart.
rules.check: Chart and table use the same selected-period model, units, source identities and missing-value semantics.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Make comparisons like for like
rules.requirement: Name both periods, their coverage and any calculation behind a change or saving claim.
rules.check: Partial and complete periods are not compared as if equal; percentage calculations handle zero and missing baselines.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Use meaningful document structure
rules.requirement: Give a page a clear main heading, use a logical heading hierarchy, and use real lists and table relationships instead of visual imitation.
rules.check: The reading order, headings, lists and table headers remain meaningful without styling.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Make meaning independent of colour and position
rules.requirement: Include text or another accessible distinction for important states and instructions; do not rely only on colour, shape, location or sound.
rules.check: States and actions remain understandable in monochrome, without icons and when read by assistive technology.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Write useful alternatives for meaningful images
rules.requirement: Describe the information or function needed for the task, and mark purely decorative images as decorative.
rules.check: Alternative text communicates purpose without duplicating adjacent text or inventing details absent from the image.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Write descriptive links and preserve logical order
rules.requirement: Use link text that identifies the destination or task, and keep content order meaningful for keyboard and screen-reader navigation.
rules.check: Links make sense in context and repeated generic labels have sufficient accessible context; visual rearrangement does not reverse task order.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Keep help and outcomes available to assistive technology
rules.requirement: Associate labels, hints and errors with their controls, and announce relevant changing outcomes without unnecessary repeated interruption.
rules.check: Keyboard and assistive-technology checks confirm the label, error, pending and final outcome relationships.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Provide honest, usable media and document alternatives
rules.requirement: Use structured HTML for routine guidance where practical, and supply accurate captions, transcripts and accessible document alternatives when the content requires them.
rules.check: Advertised alternatives exist, match the current content and are checked in their actual format.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Describe accessibility evidence accurately
rules.requirement: Report what was tested and any known limitations without treating a checker, checklist, score or theme as a guarantee of accessibility.
rules.check: Claims identify the scope, method and remaining manual checks; no unsupported certification is implied.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Record ownership, sources and scope
rules.requirement: Give authored guidance an owner or review responsibility, a meaningful version/date record and the sources or implementation evidence behind its claims.
rules.check: The review record identifies the content, relevant version, evidence and responsible review route.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Explain changes that alter meaning
rules.requirement: Write a change note that says what changed and how it affects the task when behaviour, scope or interpretation changes.
rules.check: A reader can identify the relevant difference without comparing entire versions.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Keep editorial dates separate from device dates
rules.requirement: Label publication, content update, content review and data timestamps according to what actually happened.
rules.check: A review date is not automatically advanced by a build, and it cannot be confused with a device reading or service record.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Record exceptions and confirmed findings
rules.requirement: For an applicable rule, record pass, finding, not applicable or a justified SHOULD deviation with evidence; propose any MUST contract change explicitly.
rules.check: Every finding links a stable rule ID to specific copy or behaviour and has a concrete acceptance check.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Review facts, language and presentation separately
rules.requirement: Check the technical truth first, then wording and structure, then the rendered result with realistic data and relevant users.
rules.check: Review evidence covers factual accuracy, read-aloud wording, state scenarios and the actual rendered layout.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Report validation within its limits
rules.requirement: Separate source review, automated checks, manual interaction checks, user research and live-device verification in the evidence record.
rules.check: A result never claims an unperformed check or a broader scope than the evidence supports.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

source_conflicts.resolution: Expanded negative and critical-condition forms; positive contractions only when clear for the audience. Native translations remain intact.
Use scores and length as diagnostic prompts; task comprehension and correctness decide.
Preserve HA precision, units, timezone and locale; do not import NHS clinical thresholds, general rounding or UK clock defaults.
Descriptive headings for explanatory articles; genuine questions remain valid form labels and legends.
Preserve Notifications, Entity ID, Turn on and other actual translated labels despite generic glossary preferences.
Do not import old print point sizes or restrictions that would remove web link underlines; web tokens and accessible interaction apply.
No clinical assurance, immigration rules, official identity or external endorsement transferred.

excluded_topics.source: NHS inclusive skin symptoms and clinical A–Z entries
excluded_topics.reason: Clinical content does not define household device states, diagnoses or safety thresholds.

excluded_topics.source: Home Office immigration and legal status instructions
excluded_topics.reason: Not a household permission or eligibility model.

excluded_topics.source: Plain English website/readability PDFs inaccessible during review
